name: '95 Grotti Cheetah
summary: A mid-1990s Grotti sports car that comes with the Ultimate Edition, in a pared-back retro-futuristic livery.
body: Rockstar's Ultimate Edition description calls it Grotti's signature sports car of the mid '90s and a tribute to Shore Drive, and says it becomes available for later-stage action.
Its in-game class, performance and price have not been published.
GTABase's page for the Grotti Cheetah '95 lists a registration cost of $32,750 and a stolen sell value of $16,775.
GTABase says it carries an Advanced Tracker.
GTABase lists its specialist type as Luxury.
In-game stat bars (out of 10): Speed 6.6, Acceleration 5.9, Asphalt handling 6.5, Off-road handling 4.4, Strength 3.0, as read by GTABase only so far.

facts.price: $32,750 (Story Mode price, which the guides read as the registration cost)
facts.where: Ultimate Edition: Chapter 5: after Honest Abe, Pegassi Residences, lift opposite the entrance to Parking B1 (Push Square UE guide).
facts.customise: Specialist tag "Luxury" (GTABase) matches the Luxury specialty shop: Euroform Automotive

name: '55 Vapid Stanier
summary: A two-tone 1950s Vapid sedan that is part of the Vintage Vice City Pack, along with a garage by Ocean Beach.
body: Rockstar lists the car and its garage among the pack's contents, next to outfits and hairstyles for Jason and Lucia and a weapon pattern.
Nothing has been published about how it drives.
Jalopnik says players who qualify for the Vintage Vice City Pack get a task in the Exploration tab of the map that leads to the Ocean View Hotel, where the car and its garage are waiting.

Jalopnik describes the car as two-tone yellow on white and sees it as a nod to the 1955 Oldsmobile Super 88 parked outside the Avalon Hotel on Miami's Ocean Drive, though the game's car has a hardtop rather than a convertible roof.
Jalopnik says the pack is a pre-order bonus that can still be had by ordering before the end of November 19.

facts.where: Ultimate Edition: Chapter 3: Ocean View Hotel, Vice Beach, after a map marker appears; getting in gives the Shore Court garage (Push Square UE guide).

name: Vapid Ganado
summary: Jason's well-worn, low-riding pickup. The Ultimate Edition adds the Ganado Retro Build, a set of exclusive mods for it.
body: Rockstar describes the Retro Build as adding muscle and classic styling to the truck. One of its images shows Jason driving a Ganado in yellow paint with a red racing stripe.

IGN says the Ultimate Edition Retro Build for Jason's Vapid '70 Ganado is claimed at Coastal Auto Care, whose owner Joey texts its location shortly after Chapter 1 begins, adding a Fix Your Car objective that IGN says slightly raises Jason's relationship with Lucia.
IGN says the required repairs, including the engine and a respray, come first; the build is then under Pro Builds, Full Kits, as Retro Build: Ultimate Edition.
IGN says the Retro Build is more than a cosmetic change, giving the Ganado slightly better speed and acceleration.
Game8 says Jason's '70 Ganado is obtained after the first main mission, Gone Fishing, parked at Brian's marina; it gives 2 seats, a Muscle specialist, speed 4.7 and acceleration 5.3.

Eurogamer says the Retro Build is claimed at Coastal Auto Care during Fix Your Car, after the repair and respray, under Pro Builds > Full Kits > 'Retro Build: Ultimate Edition', and that it slightly raises speed and acceleration.
Eurogamer's report on Ultimate Edition unlocks says the retro Ganado, like Jason's other safehouse vehicles, is usable only during Chapter 1.
GTABase's page for the Vapid Ganado '70 lists a registration cost of $6,500 and a stolen sell value of $1,980.
GTABase says it carries no tracker.
In-game stat bars (out of 10): Speed 4.7, Acceleration 5.3, Asphalt handling 3.6, Off-road handling 4.5, Strength 3.0, read from the game by two sources.

With the Retro Build - Standard fitted (exclusive, $1,535, needs a bank account), an in-game screenshot shows the bars at Speed 4.8, Acceleration 5.4, Asphalt handling 3.9, Off-road handling 4.2 and Strength 3.0, with the asphalt rating up 21 to 479 (class A) and the other rating down 12 to 318. Liveries: Vintage Stripes and Street Raider.

facts.price: $6,500 (Story Mode price, which the guides read as the registration cost)

name: Shitzu Squalo
summary: A boat in a pink-to-blue gradient that comes with the Ultimate Edition, docked at Washington Beach.
body: Rockstar pitches it for fishing in Gambit Bay, and says it is made ready for open water by a weapons crate loaded with explosives.
GameSpot says Ultimate Edition owners can take a custom Shitzu Squalo from just after Chapter 4 begins, docked on Washington Island near the Y Hotel, and that it stays there for most of the story.
Game8 lists a separate Fine Art variant, the Street Art Squalo, on a trailer on Sunset Dr in Key Lento.

facts.where: Ultimate Edition: Chapter 4: docked on Atlantic Ave, Washington Beach, Vice Beach, just east of the Y Hotel (Push Square UE guide).

name: Dinka Enduro
summary: A motorcycle in Army-fatigue colours, one of the two safehouse vehicles for Jason in the Ultimate Edition.
body: Rockstar lists it with the Crest Kayak under Jason's Safehouse Vehicles.
IGN calls it the Dinka '72 Enduro and says this Ultimate Edition motorcycle is stored underneath Jason's Key Lento house.
Eurogamer, citing IGN's unlock details, says Jason's Ultimate Edition Dinka Enduro and Crest Kayak can only be used during Chapter 1.
In-game stat bars (out of 10): Speed 3.9, Acceleration 5.7, Asphalt handling 5.2, Off-road handling 7.6, Strength 4.0, as read by GTABase only so far.

facts.price: $2,400 (Story Mode price, which the guides read as the registration cost)
facts.where: GTABase: Parked here at night.; Ultimate Edition: Chapter 1: underneath Jason's house in Key Lento (Push Square UE guide).
facts.customise: Specialist tag "Dirt Bike" (GTABase) matches the Dirt Bike specialty shop: Dirt Merchants

name: Crest Kayak
summary: A kayak, one of the two safehouse vehicles for Jason in the Ultimate Edition.
body: Rockstar lists it with the Dinka Enduro motorcycle under Jason's Safehouse Vehicles. One of its images shows an orange one.
Eurogamer, citing IGN's unlock details, says the Ultimate Edition Crest Kayak, like the Dinka Enduro, can only be used during Chapter 1.
